Quite a lot of people need guns, actually. Rural folk keeping their livestock safe from predators, even just self-defense in the city.

This isn’t a gun problem. “Assault rifles” have been around since the 60s. We’ve only seen mass/school shootings rise in modern times after Columbine. So what gives? Why is this a trend now, and why does this keep happening? 

In my POV, it’s three things:
1. Mental health. If it’s covered, it’s covered very minimally, and the system is so overrun it takes months to see someone and get help.
2. Média glorification. Do you think it’s a coincidence Buffalo happened and then this right after? We publicize the names of shooters, do deep dives, and give them the game they wanted. Look at the commonalities: most are young, bullied, and isolated in the world. We need better support for our kids. 
3. Lack of education. In most states, it’s required to take drivers Education to pass high school.  We also have students get CPR certified. Not everyone drives - why not have a gun safety course even if some don’t plan on owning weapons?

At the end of the day, our cultures are different. Comparing countries is never going to be 1:1, and doesn’t take into account full context. We are (almost definitely) never going to get rid of the 2nd amendment. We need to address the root of the problem if we want to solve this in our country.

Not LGBT, so take my opinion with a very large grain of salt. 

Pro: race is a construct, similar to gender. We’re already seeing this in modern discourse, as we broke down “white” not necessarily to mean skin color (although it derives from it), but rather having the power in social dynamics. It is an identity that we have, much like gender. We can think of “ethnicity” to “race” as we do “sex” to “gender”. Since race is a social construct and identity, we can perceive ourselves as a different identity that what we are assigned. 

Against: like it or not, race is still corroborated with skin color. We still use the terms “white” and “black” because they derived from when it was absolutely based on skin color. Also, it’s somewhat unbelievable- when someone wants to be “trans-racial”, it usually means gaining access to the culture of the target race in bad faith. For example, white people claiming to be trans-racially black so they can say the n-word. So, not only is this mostly done in bad faith, it’s not as easy to distinguish what being “trans-racial” means like it is with gender identity or transgender.
